pr_body:
Following are the fixes that have been applied:

- Add backticks using `heredoc.Docf` wherever needed for `Long` and `Annotations`
- Remove trailing whitespace
- Use `[]` for args instead of `{}` in `Use` to be consistent with the rest
- Fix indentation
- Use `<>` for links as mentioned #8404 
  - Fixes #8404
- Fix examples like this:
  ```shell
  # Description
  $ gh ...
  ```
- Rewrap very long lines in shorter ones
- Rearrange command fields as `Use`, `Short`, `Long`, `Example`, `Args`, ...

issue_context.title: Standardise markup for URLs in docs
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

> Something I realized over the course of this PR is that URLs formatted with `<` and `>` are the only variants that get turned into links on the CLI manual website.
> 
> Rather than extending this PR further, that might be a great follow up to review that behavior and align it.
> 
> _Originally posted by @andyfeller in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/8342#discussion_r1412121749_

### Proposed solution

Another round of checking current manual webpages or markers in code base one by one.

### Additional context

From my memory of proposing #8342, the most un-marked case is `github.com`, which is usually used to denote the `HOST`.

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b215d03e7b5990ea35bc0870a55d7b84f5d8c987/pkg/cmd/extension/command.go#L303-L304
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b215d03e7b5990ea35bc0870a55d7b84f5d8c987/pkg/cmd/search/code/code.go#L42-L44
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/b215d03e7b5990ea35bc0870a55d7b84f5d8c987/pkg/cmd/root/help_topic.go#L45-L47

review_comments: Similar to the `gh gist delete` comment above, I'm unsure what the right thing to do here is.

```suggestion
			For more information on git credential helpers, see
```

I think there is probably a different way we can phrase this as I'm not sure either side is simple and clear.

```suggestion
			By default, runs are fetched from active workflows.
			
			To fetch runs from disabled workflows, use %[1]s-a, --all%[1]s flag.
```

```suggestion
			For more information on OAuth scopes, see
```

Keeping the language here closer to the `Short` phrasing:

```suggestion
			Print the authentication token for an account on a given GitHub host.
```

```suggestion
			- a container image URI (e.g. %[1]soci://<image-uri>%[1]s)
			  (must already be authenticated with container registry for OCI URLs)
```
Wanting to return to long mode

I know this was just moved for general consistency.  Again this PR is already large, but I wonder if flags in messages like this should be inline quoted, too.

_Not suggesting increasing scope; making observation_

Aside from restoring the long `Example`, if we're touching this then we should consider adding a `Long` section that explains how this clears out cached API request data and whatever else is included.

I honestly don't know what the right thing to do here is as [POSIX utility](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap12.html) standard doesn't really address required forms, the brackets generally mean optional whereas one of these is required.
I realize we have other commands that use this syntax for different argument variants, but mixing argument and flag feels weird.

So, I think this needs to change a little bit more because I first thought there were typos here `numbers`/`urls` but this commands actually does take multiple.  However the usage statement doesn't really communicate it in POSIX style

Outside of making this note stand out completely on its own, would shortening like this make sense?

```suggestion
			- a container image URI (e.g. %[1]soci://<image-uri>%[1]s)
			  (must already be authenticated with container registry for OCI URLs)
```

Aside from the long example, there is a weird undiscussed observation from maintainers where some extension authors and people are setting things that are not actually official core `gh` configurations.  If we decide to touch this, then having a `Long` here or somewhere that explains what people should expect with configuration; maybe this live in the root `config` command 🤔

Minor tweak to keep this more inline with [GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en) language:

```suggestion
			For more information on OAuth scopes, see
```

The thing I don't understand just looking at the changes is how you're determining some of these lines should be wrapped versus not.  This is something I'd feel more comfortable with maintainers having the decision deciding with insight from contributors.  To note, the line above isn't wrapped, so I'm unsure how important this is to address here and how we'd do it if we decided to.

Wow, okay little bit of a rabbit hole approach to subcommandset.

Again, would love seeing this expanded into long form with a comment:

```suggestion
		Example: heredocs.Doc(`
			# Open HTTP(80) traffic to org members and HTTP(8000) traffic to public, make HTTP(3000) private
			$ gh codespace ports visibility 80:org 3000:private 8000:public",
		`),
```

```suggestion
			For information on configuring default branch, see
```

I like the idea of quoting these variables and meaningful strings.  My only concern that I'm going to do some local testing is the result of these changes.
